summary: Nyingcha Duoji works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Boston University and completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under Mark Elliott.

Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche (1932–1999) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Nyoshul Monastery (~1944) and Katok Monastery, and under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Nyoten Jinbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Ogyen Trinley Dorje (born 1985) is a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama (~2000), Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (~2001), Pema Donyo Nyinje, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, and Bokar Rinpoche.
Ohryu Matsushima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and later held a post there.

Olaf Hansen (1902–1969) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937–1945), the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1969), and the University of Jena.

Olav Hackstein (born 1962) specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UPenn and the University of Freiburg, later holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg, UPenn, EPHE, and a chair at the University of Munich (2008).

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2004–2009) under Ernst Steinkellner and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton (PhD ~1955), he held posts at ASOR, the University of Michigan, Harvard, and IAS.

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He served as Secretary at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS (PhD under William Stede), later heading Sanskrit at Ceylon and holding posts at Pennsylvania and Harvard.

Oliver Hellwig works in Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. He completed his habilitation under Harry Falk and held posts at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf and the University of Zurich (attested 2024–2025).
Oliver Petersen (born 1961) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang (~1983–2003) and held a post at the Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg beginning around 1983.
Oliver Philipp Frey is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and later held an academic post there.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris, where he later held a post (~1959–1970) before teaching at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Pierre L. Lamant. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1990) and as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2001–2002).

Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Copenhagen, Harvard, and the University of Washington, completed doctoral work under Tord Olsson, and held a post at Lund University (attested 2000–2007).
Olli Littunen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who is a PhD candidate at Leiden University (attested 2026) under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop.

Om Prakash is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and held positions at Kirori Mal College, the University of Delhi, and the Delhi School of Economics.
